title: Offline supply-chain validation and network-quarantine acceptance criteria for VPC deployments
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Purpose: Define explicit requirements and measurable acceptance criteria for Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments that must operate with zero or strictly scheduled egress (air-gapped or near-air-gapped). This ticket captures the product-level decisions for supply-chain validation, network-quarantine controls during upgrades, and operatorless bootstrap constraints so that engineering can implement deterministic test harnesses and runbooks.

Background: Customers in regulated industries require predictable, auditable upgrades with minimal external connectivity. Existing PRDs focus on staged image mirroring and operator rollback, but lack a compact, testable set of failure modes and artifact-validation gates that can be executed without any cloud-side callbacks. This document scopes the minimum product acceptance gate set that the Private product must satisfy for the 2025.04 release.

Scope:
- Required: artifact provenance & signature validation, deterministic offline canary simulation, egress-window orchestration, mirror fallback with throttled replication, KMS key rotation preflight without cloud calls.
- Out of scope: shipping an alternate CD pipeline; deep integration with customer NMS consoles (will be follow-up).

Goals:
1) Provide engineering with clear, testable acceptance criteria they can run in CI or customer-like labs.
2) Reduce post-upgrade incidents by enforcing signed artifact and manifest checks.
3) Ensure safe operatorless bootstrap paths for fully-isolated sites (no egress) and a graduated fallback when limited egress is permitted.
acceptance_criteria: Artifact provenance: All operator images and packages accepted by the Private operator must include a signed digest and provenance file. During an offline upgrade test, the operator must reject unsigned or tampered artifacts with an explicit error code and human-readable remediation steps.

Deterministic offline canary: A simulated canary run (local Vagrant/K8s kind test harness) must be able to execute the full upgrade flow using mirrored artifacts only, and produce a pass/fail report with diffs for operator state (ready pods, CRs applied, and post-upgrade healthchecks).

Egress-window enforcement: The system must support a scheduled egress window with start/end times and enforced connection counts. If upgrade steps require temporary outbound access, the operator must pause and present a re-try strategy; after three failed window attempts, the operator must roll back to a previously recorded checkpoint.

Mirror fallback: If primary mirror checksum mismatch is detected, the operator must (a) consult the local mirror registry snapshot, (b) attempt a secondary mirror on the same network, and (c) if both fail, enter a safe rollback state without partial apply. All mirror decisions must be logged to local audit logs with signatures.

KMS preflight: For key rotation or KMS-bound upgrades, the operator must validate locally cached wrapping keys and be able to perform an upgrade dry-run that demonstrates secret unseal and re-seal without contacting external KMS endpoints. Dry-run success required for release acceptance.

Operatorless bootstrap acceptance: A new-node bootstrap flow that receives a pre-seeded, signed bootstrap bundle must be able to join the cluster and reach 'Ready' state entirely within the isolated network. Errors must include deterministic retry semantics and time-based backoff in logs.

Telemetry and audit: During offline tests, the operator must emit a compact telemetry artifact that can be exported after the fact (tarball of logs + signed manifest). The artifact must contain timestamps and unambiguous step identifiers for postmortem analysis.

Security rejection paths: Any deviation from signed-manifest validation must result in non-silent failure paths; acceptance requires explicit non-ambiguous CLI/console messages with next-step guidance for operators.

Canary pass rate: In a staged fleet of 5 representative nodes, the offline canary must pass end-to-end checks in at least 4/5 nodes; failures must have automated collection of evidence and be annotated in the canary report.
constraints: No external package registries assumed during offline tests (all artifacts must be mirrored).
Network partitions during upgrade simulation must be reproducible via the test harness (scripted partition scenarios).
All artifacts must be signed using customer-provided or operator-generated keys; trust anchors need to be configurable in the operator profile.
Where minimal egress is permitted, the operator must limit outbound endpoints to a customer-configurable allowlist and report attempted-but-blocked egress in audit logs.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 - Lab validation: Engineering runs the deterministic offline canary harness against two internal clusters (single-site isolated and limited-egress simulated) and generates signed test artifacts.
Phase 2 - Alpha: Offer to three pilot customers under NDA; run controlled upgrades with mirrored artifacts and collect telemetry tarballs for analysis.
Phase 3 - Beta: Expand pilots to 10 customers, add automated rollback triggers and integrate KMS dry-run into preflight checklist.
Phase 4 - Production release: Bake acceptance gates into the Private operator image release pipeline and require passing dry-run reports in the release checklist.
telemetry_requirements: Compact offline report format (JSONL) that includes step_id, status, start_ts, end_ts, node_id, and signed checksum of applied artifacts.
Audit log entries must be locally retained for a configurable retention window (default 90 days) and support export to customer's SIEM after upgrade.
Healthchecks must include a deterministic list: pod_ready_count, cr_sync_state, kv_cache_integrity, and network_quarantine_status.
notes: Trade-offs: Full offline proofing increases test complexity; we prefer a small deterministic harness over a broad brittle emulation of all customer networks.
Decision: Require signed manifests by default; allow customer opt-out only with an explicit risk waiver reviewed by security and CSM.
Open: Define exact rollback checkpoints and how stateful workloads are reconciled post-rollback (engineering to propose safe-state model).
success_metrics: Offline canary pass rate >= 80% across pilot customers before GA.
No security incidents related to artifact tampering during pilot upgrades.
Mean time to detect mirror checksum mismatch < 5 minutes in harness reports.
Customer-reported upgrade pain points reduced by 60% in pilot feedback surveys.
